claim: The binary arm of NullPropagatedOperands has no operator filter, so AndAlso/OrElse operands are treated as null-propagating and DropNotNullChecks deletes a load-bearing IS NOT NULL guard, producing wrong query results.
raw: The unary arm at `:621-622` is carefully allow-listed to `Not`/`Negate`/`Convert`. The binary arm has no operator filter, but `SqlBinaryExpression.IsValidOperator` (`src/EFCore.Relational/Query/SqlExpressions/SqlBinaryExpression.cs:93,95`) admits `AndAlso` and `OrElse`, for which the optimization's premise (`X IS NULL ⇒ result IS NULL`) is false: `NULL AND FALSE = FALSE`, `NULL OR TRUE = TRUE`.

claim: No new test covers a logical-operator result (&&, ||, ??, or an equality expanded by null semantics), leaving the entire vulnerable operator class untested.
raw:
### 2. No test covers any logical-operator result — the entire vulnerable class is untested
`test/EFCore.Relational.Specification.Tests/Query/NullSemanticsQueryTestBase.cs:2250-2293`

The five new tests use only `~` (Not) and `+` (Add/concat). No test has `clause.Result` be `&&`, `||`, `??`, or an equality that expands via null semantics. ... That is why only 6 baseline files needed updating and why nothing turned red.

claim: There is no negative test asserting the CASE guard is retained when it must be, so a future widening of the optimization would produce no baseline churn and no failure signal.
raw: All five new tests are "the optimization fires" tests. `Is_not_null_optimizes_binary_op_with_mixed_checks` (`:2288`) keeps a CASE only because of a leftover unrelated conjunct, not because a guard was correctly refused. Four of the five assert fully-collapsed SQL, so a future widening (invited by the `// TODO` at `:577`) would produce no baseline churn in these tests at all

claim: SqlFunctionExpression's ArgumentsPropagateNullability/InstancePropagatesNullability flags are silently promoted from an optimization hint to a correctness contract, and dropping the guard hoists the call out of the CASE so it is now evaluated with NULL arguments.
raw: A provider or `HasTranslation` that mis-declares `ArgumentsPropagateNullability` previously produced a suboptimal expansion; it now produces wrong rows. Dropping the guard also hoists the function call out of the CASE, so it is evaluated with NULL arguments on rows where it previously was not — relevant for scalar UDFs that throw on NULL. No new test uses a function result; coverage is incidental

claim: The new function arm re-implements the null-propagation traversal already present in ProcessNullNotNull and diverges from it (unguarded Instance! dereference, and looping over ArgumentsPropagateNullability.Count instead of Arguments.Count).
raw:
The new function arm re-implements the traversal already in `ProcessNullNotNull`, with two divergences beyond the Critical one:
- `:634` uses `if (func.InstancePropagatesNullability == true)` then dereferences `func.Instance!`; the sibling at `:2394` guards with `is { Instance: not null, InstancePropagatesNullability: true }`. ... Extracting one shared helper would have prevented finding #1 entirely.

claim: The soundness precondition of the new transform is undocumented; the one-line comment understates what it does and never states the load-bearing invariant.
raw: `// optimize expressions such as expr != null ? expr : null` understates the transform — it handles multi-conjunct tests, partial conjunct removal, and transitive descent through unary/binary/function trees. The load-bearing invariant ("every node kind descended into must return NULL when the descended-into operand is NULL") is unstated, which is precisely why the binary arm's missing filter reads as an oversight rather than a decision.

claim: DropNotNullChecks uses a null return value as a 'true' sentinel with no contract comment, so a later bail-out returning null would silently delete the whole WHEN test with no compiler signal.
raw: `src/EFCore.Relational/Query/SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:600` (`return null; // true`), consumed at `:585` and `:607-609`. A `SqlExpression?` returning `null` reads as "could not process". If anyone later adds a bail-out returning `null`, the whole `WHEN` test is silently deleted and every row takes the THEN branch — a wrong-results bug with no compiler signal.

claim: The helpers are static local functions inside VisitCase rather than protected virtual members, so a provider hit by the defect cannot override or opt out of the rewrite, and nothing signals that it fired.
raw: The helpers are `static` **local** functions inside `VisitCase`, outside the `protected virtual` surface that `SqlNullabilityProcessor` otherwise exposes (34 members, subclassed by `SqlServerSqlNullabilityProcessor`). A provider hitting finding #1 can only override the whole ~90-line `VisitCase` or set `UseRelationalNulls` (far broader). Nothing signals that the rewrite fired — the CASE is simply absent.

claim: IsNull returns false for a C# null elseResult, so the no-ELSE form CASE WHEN t THEN r END is skipped while the equivalent ... ELSE NULL END is folded.
raw: `src/EFCore.Relational/Query/SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:578`. `IsNull` (`:1633`) returns `false` for a C# `null` `elseResult`, so `CASE WHEN t THEN r END` is skipped while the identical `... ELSE NULL END` is folded — even though `:571` (`elseResult ?? Constant(null, …)`) and `:561` already encode the equivalence. Fix: `(elseResult is null || IsNull(elseResult))`. Missed optimization only, not a correctness issue.

claim: RestoreNullValueColumnsList is called with currentNonNullableColumnsCount instead of currentNullValueColumnsCount, corrupting the _nullValueColumns state the new optimization depends on (pre-existing, not introduced by this PR).
raw: `src/EFCore.Relational/Query/SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:539`: `RestoreNullValueColumnsList(currentNonNullableColumnsCount);` passes the non-nullable count to the null-value restore. `:529` and `:566` both correctly pass `currentNullValueColumnsCount`. **Confirmed present at base `051c33a79` — not introduced here**, but it corrupts the `_nullValueColumns` state feeding the result-visiting this change now depends on.

claim: Building nullPropagatedOperands inserts every node of the result subtree into a HashSet whose GetHashCode is recursive and uncached, giving O(n^2) hashing cost per translation.
raw: `src/EFCore.Relational/Query/SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:580`. Every node of the result subtree is inserted into a `HashSet<SqlExpression>`, and `GetHashCode` is recursive and uncached (`SqlBinaryExpression.cs:172-173`). Per-translation cost only (translations are cached), gated behind a cheap `IsNull` check. Track, don't block.

claim: Claim that the ?? / Coalesce path is broken in practice by the same optimization — refuted, since the factory emits a SqlFunctionExpression with [false, false] so the CASE is correctly kept.
raw: - **`??` / `Coalesce` is broken in practice** — no. `IntA != null ? (IntA ?? 0) : null` correctly keeps its `CASE`, because the factory emits a `SqlFunctionExpression` with `[false, false]`. Only reachable via `MakeBinary`.

claim: Claim of an index mismatch between ArgumentsPropagateNullability and Arguments — refuted, the constructor throws InconsistentNumberOfArguments.
raw: - **Index mismatch between `ArgumentsPropagateNullability` and `Arguments`** — the constructor throws `InconsistentNumberOfArguments` (`SqlFunctionExpression.cs:216-226`).

claim: Claim that IsNull(elseResult) throws on a null elseResult — refuted, the signature accepts SqlExpression? and returns false.
raw: - **`IsNull(elseResult)` throws on a null `elseResult`** — signature is `IsNull(SqlExpression?)`; it returns `false`.

claim: Claim that shaping SQL on a runtime parameter value breaks query caching — refuted, parameter nullability is part of the second-level cache key so DoNotCache() is not required.
raw: - **Shaping SQL on a runtime parameter value breaks caching** — parameter nullability is part of the 2nd-level cache key; `:1631` documents this and `DoNotCache()` is correctly not required.

claim: Claim that the nullable out-parameter is wrong on the early-return path — refuted, IsNull(elseResult) implies elseResultNullable so nullable is already true.
raw: - **`nullable` out-param wrong on the early-return path** — `IsNull(elseResult)` implies `elseResultNullable`, so `nullable` is already `true`.

claim: Claim that CLR Type / TypeMapping drifts when returning clause.Result directly — refuted by testing StrA != null ? (int?)StrA.Length : null.
raw: - **CLR `Type`/`TypeMapping` drift on `return clause.Result`** — tested `StrA != null ? (int?)StrA.Length : null`; correct.

claim: Claim that the CASE operand is discarded on the early return — refuted, the path is guarded by testIsCondition which requires caseExpression.Operand == null.
raw: - **`operand` discarded on the early return** — guarded by `testIsCondition`, which is `caseExpression.Operand == null`.

claim: Claim that HashSet structural equality could over-match operands — refuted, ColumnExpression equality includes IsNullable making it stricter (miss-only).
raw: - **`HashSet` structural equality could over-match** — `ColumnExpression` equality includes `IsNullable`, making it stricter; miss-only.

claim: Claim that the new TODO without an issue link violates project convention — refuted, the same file has three other unlinked TODOs and ~75% of TODOs under src/EFCore.Relational/ are unlinked.
raw: - **`TODO` without an issue link violates convention** — `SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs` has three other unlinked TODOs (`:2173`, `:2181`, `:2208`); ~75% of TODOs under `src/EFCore.Relational/` are unlinked.

claim: Claim that the row sets returned by WHERE change under the optimization — not reproduced; the verified impact is on projected values only.
raw: - **Row sets returned by `WHERE` change** — I could not reproduce this; the one filter case I built kept its guard. Verified impact is on **projected values**.
